judge_assessment.explanation: The rejection is warranted but both hard failures overstate what the worksheet prints. "Every problem requires selecting linear, quadratic, or piecewise and justifying the model from contextual evidence" is not what the stems say. In problem 1 the classification AND its evidence are GIVEN ("The first differences are equal, so a linear model fits"); in problem 3 the model is handed over outright ("the model that fits is h(t) = -16t^2+64t"). Problems 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10 ask for a number or a solution set and nothing else, and each of those printed slots IS verified - including problem 9's pair (8, 84) and problem 10's two intersections (1,4) and (5,12), both covered by `system` entries. The second hard failure is likewise wrong that "model-choice explanations recur throughout all 12 problems": only problems 6(b), 11 and 12(c) demand prose, and two of those three ALREADY carry manual entries with stated acceptance criteria. What is genuinely defective is narrower: problem 11 ("Explain what Rae's evidence actually shows about the model") has only an eval (89) and no manual entry - a real instance of the batch's dominant failure; and problems 1 and 6(a) both say "write the model" while only the value derived from it is checked. There is also a sheet-level mismatch the judge did not name but which is the strongest support for its claim: the directions box says "Say what your evidence is, then build the model, then answer", a blanket demand that most stems do not repeat, the key does not grade, and nothing checks. Every keyed value is correct - I recomputed 115, 10, 28, {0,4}, 13, 52, 8, {10,20}, (8,84), (1,4) and (5,12), 89, 20 and 16.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 12 is the per-slot discipline done right: three entries under one id - `eval` for the 10-mile fare (20), `solve` for the 27.50 fare (16 miles), and `manual` for part (c) with an acceptance criterion that names the answer's substance ("the rate of change is 2 dollars per mile up to 6 miles and 1.25 after that, so the graph is two connected segments with a corner at 6 miles"). Problem 6(b)'s manual desc is equally specific (constant FIRST differences of 5, versus a quadratic's changing first differences with constant second differences).

The piecewise thread is built to be re-entered rather than repeated: problem 5 evaluates the garage fare forward (5 hours -> 13 dollars) and problem 7 inverts the SAME model (22 dollars -> 8 hours), then problem 12 does both directions on a two-rate fare with a flag drop. That is genuine interleaving, not a second instance of one skeleton.

Problems 9 and 10 both use `system` checks that verify BOTH coordinates (and, for the quadratic-linear pair, both intersection points), so the compare-models facet has complete coverage of everything it prints.

The four declared traps encode the same misconception from four angles - reading a first difference as a constant rate - with derived numbers: 40*6 = 240, 48*3.5 = 168, f + r*t = 19 (charging the hourly rate for all five hours), and 5 + 4*6 = 29, which is exactly the prediction problem 11 attributes to Rae.

Problem 11's construction is the sharpest item on the sheet: the planted wrong prediction (29) is DECLARED as a trap and coincides with the table's own year-3 value, so a student who extends linearly lands on a number that looks plausible against the data.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says it plainly - "Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer" - but line 249 immediately narrows it ("Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning") and tells the author to reframe error analysis "via the ordinary types". Read together, the guidance reads as a licence to type an explanation-bearing problem by its numeric half. Nothing in the gate chain notices, because no gate reads the problem prose looking for a demanded explanation. On this sheet the machinery is clearly understood - ids 6 and 12 carry manual entries with real acceptance criteria - so the failure is one missed application (id 11) rather than an absent practice.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's verification contract has a per-PROBLEM floor, not a per-RESPONSE-SLOT floor: "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". A multi-part sheet therefore satisfies the gate with one scalar per id, and build.sh prints "0 manual" - which reads as "everything on this sheet was checked" rather than "every id had something checked". Two printed slots here go uncovered: problem 1 says "Write the model, then use it to find the total cost" and only the cost (115) is checked; problem 6(a) says "Decide which kind of model fits, write it, and predict the depth" and only the depth (52) is checked. Separately, the directions box demands a written evidence statement on every problem that neither the stems, the key, nor the verify file honours - a blanket demand should either be dropped or represented by a declared check.

improvements.title: Apply the existing manual practice to every stem that demands prose
improvements.proposed_change: This file already declares manual entries with acceptance criteria on ids 6 and 12; the fix is to make the practice mandatory rather than discretionary. Add the prose lint in tests/check_layout.py (stems containing "explain", "say what", "describe", "how do you know") so a demanded explanation without a manual entry is reported. Here that is one added entry on id 11: "Rae used a single first difference as a constant rate; the first differences 4, 8, 12 are not constant while the SECOND differences (4) are, so the model is quadratic, not linear." That sentence already exists in the answer key.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 3 reads "Explain what the evidence shows about the model, then use P(t) to find the value at t = 6" with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 3. Assert the gate chain lists problem 3 as manual; today it exits 0 for that stem.
improvements.expected_impact: The one missed explanation joins the two already-declared ones, taking this sheet's manual count from 2 to 3 and closing the actual verification gap the judge was pointing at.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over problem prose will fire on stems that use "explain" inside a hint rather than as a demand. Ship it as exit 2 (manual-review visibility), which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: "Write the model" is a printed answer slot and needs its own check
improvements.proposed_change: Two parts. (1) When a stem asks the student to WRITE a model or formula before using it, add an `equiv` entry on that expression beside the eval - here, id 1 gains equiv on "25 + 15*h" and id 6 gains equiv on "5*x + 2" - so the expression the student must produce is inside the boundary, not just the number it yields. Extend the slot counter in tests/check_layout.py (see the systemic version of this issue) to count "write the model/rule/formula" as a slot. (2) Reconcile the directions box with the stems: a sheet-level demand ("Say what your evidence is") must either be dropped or carried by a declared check, so the worksheet does not ask for work that nothing grades.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 reads "Write the model, then use it to find the cost of 6 hours" with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry. Assert the layout gate reports an uncovered response slot for problem 1; it passes once an equiv entry on the model expression is added. Today the fixture passes silently.
improvements.expected_impact: The modelling half of a modelling worksheet - the expression itself - becomes verified rather than inferred from the number it produces, and the sheet's blanket directions stop demanding ungraded work.
improvements.risk: Low for part (1): equiv entries on author-supplied model expressions are cheap and cannot weaken any existing check. Part (2) is editorial and needs care so that useful strategy guidance is not stripped from directions boxes wholesale.

case_summary: Twelve correct, well-chosen modelling problems - I recomputed every keyed value including both intersections in problem 10 - with genuine interleaving (the garage fare is evaluated forward in problem 5 and inverted in problem 7), four derived traps all aimed at reading a first difference as a constant rate, and two manual entries whose descs state real acceptance criteria. I part company with the judge on scope: the worksheet does NOT require a classification and justification on every problem - problems 1 and 3 hand the model to the student, and seven others ask only for a number or a solution set, each of which is verified. The genuine defects are narrower: problem 11 demands an explanation of Rae's evidence with no manual entry; problems 1 and 6(a) tell the student to write the model while only the derived value is checked; and the directions box demands a written evidence statement on every problem that neither the stems nor the key nor the verifier honours. REJECT still stands on the problem-11 miss, but the charge as written is broader than the artefact.
